summary: E-commerce aggregator platform (e-Com Aggr. Services) with product/service listing, mock scraper, order API, contact page with iframe, and sitemap generation. Staged implementation: Stage 1 complete (routes, models, mock data), Stage 2 stubbed (QRC onboarding, arbitrage functions), Stage 3 TODO (real scraping, Merkle tracing, leaderboard integration).
architectural_notes: Staged implementation: Stage 1 (full code), Stage 2 (stubs/pseudo-code), Stage 3 (TODOs)
Mock scraper uses hard-coded array instead of real HTTP calls
Order API stores basic order data without Merkle tracing or arbitrage execution yet
Contact page iframe and CORS checks are stubbed for Stage 1
Sitemap driven by pages[] array with role-based access metadata
Modular architecture: Product/Service models, order API, scraper function, arbitrage engine
QRC onboarding API validates 10-digit mobile, generates clientId = unixTimestamp + mobile10, stores in Clients collection
POST /api/orders validates clientId against Clients collection before order creation
Minimal Merkle Root scaffold: OrderTrace stores per-order SHA-256 hash and last6 chars without full Merkle tree or payout logic
Minimal arbitrage module: set_arbitrage(p1, p2) computes p3=p1-p2, get_arbitrage logs values with TODO for future payout + Merkle-root integration

existing_features.title: Create application shell with routing for five pages: / (home), /contact, /sitemap, /products, /services
Build /products page that fetches and displays all products from the Products collection with id, title, sourceUrl, price, and currency
Build /services page that fetches and displays all services from the Services collection with id, title, sourceUrl, price, and currency

Implement /contact page that reads version-controlled contact information from a backend config or table and displays an iframe placeholder for e-contract-lwf.caffeine.xyz with stubbed CORS validation
Create /sitemap page and sitemap.xml route that dynamically generates sitemap from a pages array containing path, priority, and roleAccess fields for all application routes
Create stubbed QRC onboarding flow function that generates clientId from unixTimestamp + mobile10 with QR code generation placeholder and session storage logic (Stage 2 stub with TODO comments)
Build /onboarding page with a simple form containing one input field for mobile number and a submit button that calls POST /api/onboarding/qrc with the entered mobile10 value
On successful API response, display the generated QR code image, the clientId as plain text, and a note stating "This Client ID is required for placing orders." on the /onboarding page
Store the generated clientId in browser session storage or local storage after successful onboarding for later use in order flows

On the /products page (frontend/src/pages/Products.tsx), add a 'Mock Order' button to each product card that sends a POST request to /api/orders with payload { items: [{ productId: <product.id>, quantity: 1 }] } when clicked
Display a success message (toast or inline text) when the POST /api/orders request succeeds, and display an error message when the request fails

Update the 'Mock Order' button on /products page to read clientId from browser storage (localStorage or sessionStorage) and include it in the POST /api/orders request payload as { clientId, items: [{ productId, quantity: 1 }] }
Create frontend/src/lib/arbitrage.ts module exporting set_arbitrage(p1: number, p2: number) function that computes p3 = p1 - p2 and returns object { p1, p2, p3 }

In frontend/src/lib/arbitrage.ts, export get_arbitrage(p1: number, p2: number) function that internally calls set_arbitrage, logs the resulting { p1, p2, p3 } object to console, and includes a TODO comment for future payout and Merkle-root integration

In the existing order creation flow on frontend/src/pages/Products.tsx, after computing the order total, call get_arbitrage(p1 = total, p2 = mockWholesalePrice) where mockWholesalePrice is calculated as 80% of p1 (total * 0.8)

new_feature_requests.summary: Basic app shell with routes: /, /contact, /sitemap, /products, /services
Product and Service data models with id, title, sourceUrl, price, currency, rawPayload fields
Mock scraper function with 5-10 sample products/services to fill Products[] and Services[]
Simple order model and POST /api/orders endpoint storing clientId, items[], total
/contact page with version-controlled config and iframe for e-contract-lwf.caffeine.xyz
/sitemap page and sitemap.xml with pages[] array (path, priority, roleAccess)
QRC onboarding flow (clientId = unixTimestamp + mobile10) with QR generation - Stage 2 stub
set_arbitrage(p1, p2) and get_arbitrage(p1, p2) functions - Stage 2 stub
Real external HTTP scraping - Stage 3 TODO
Merkle Root + Nonce order tracing with last-6-chars memory - Stage 3 TODO
Leaderboard integration for dynamic payout routing - Stage 3 TODO
Define backend data models for Product and Service collections with fields: id (Text), title (Text), sourceUrl (Text), price (Float), currency (Text), rawPayload (Text)
Implement internal mock scraper function that populates Products[] and Services[] from hard-coded arrays of 5-10 sample items each (no external HTTP calls)
Create Order data model with fields clientId (Text), items (Array), total (Float) and implement POST /api/orders endpoint that stores orders without Merkle tracing or payout logic

Implement stubbed arbitrage functions set_arbitrage(p1, p2) and get_arbitrage(p1, p2) with correct signatures, parameter documentation, and dummy wallet call placeholders (Stage 2 stub with TODO comments)

Add TODO comments in backend for Stage 3 features: real external HTTP scraping logic, Merkle Root + Nonce order tracing with last-6-chars memory, and leaderboard integration for dynamic payout routing

Implement POST /api/onboarding/qrc endpoint that validates mobile10 (exactly 10 digits), generates clientId from unixTimestamp + mobile10, creates QR code, stores in Clients collection, and returns clientId + QR image data
Build /onboarding page with mobile number input form that calls QRC API, displays generated QR code and clientId, and stores clientId in browser session/local storage

Create POST /api/onboarding/qrc backend endpoint that accepts JSON payload with mobile10 field (string), validates that mobile10 is exactly 10 digits, and returns HTTP 400 with { error: "Invalid mobile" } if validation fails

On successful validation, generate clientId by concatenating current Unix timestamp (as integer string) with the mobile10 value, generate a QR code image containing the clientId, store a Client record with fields clientId, mobile10, and createdAt in a Clients collection, and return JSON response with clientId and qrcImageUrlOrData fields
Add 'Mock Order' button on /products page for each product that sends POST /api/orders with single item and displays success/error message
Update POST /api/orders to require clientId in request body, validate against Clients collection, return 400 error if missing/invalid
Update /products 'Mock Order' button to read clientId from browser storage and include in POST /api/orders payload
Update POST /api/orders backend endpoint to require clientId field in the JSON request body with structure { clientId: string, items: { productId: string, quantity: number }[] }
Validate clientId by looking it up in the existing Clients collection created by the /onboarding QRC flow before creating an order
Return HTTP 400 with JSON body { error: "Unknown or missing clientId" } when clientId is missing from the request or not found in the Clients collection
When clientId is valid, create the order exactly as before with the same items processing, same mock total calculation, and same response shape
Add OrderTrace data structure with orderId, txHash, last6, createdAt fields
Implement helper to compute SHA-256 hash of order payload, store txHash and last6=txHash.slice(-6) in OrderTrace on order creation
Expose backend function/endpoint to read last6 for a given orderId
Add OrderTrace data structure to backend/main.mo with fields: orderId (Text), txHash (Text), last6 (Text), and createdAt (Int) representing Unix timestamp

Implement a deterministic hash helper function in backend/main.mo that takes the order payload (clientId and items array), converts it to a canonical string representation, and computes a SHA-256 hash returning it as a hexadecimal string

Update the createOrder function in backend/main.mo to automatically compute txHash for each new order using the hash helper, extract last6 as the last 6 characters of txHash, create an OrderTrace record with the orderId, txHash, last6, and current timestamp, and store it in the orderTraces collection

Expose a backend query function getOrderTrace(orderId: Text) in backend/main.mo that looks up and returns the last6 value for a given orderId, returning null or an error if the orderId is not found in the OrderTrace collection

Create minimal arbitrage helper module (arbitrage.ts) with set_arbitrage(p1, p2) → { p1, p2, p3=p1-p2 } and get_arbitrage(p1, p2) that logs values with TODO for future payout + Merkle-root integration
In order creation flow, call get_arbitrage(p1=total, p2=mockWholesalePrice) where mockWholesalePrice = 80% of p1, compute and log arbitrage values without real payouts or external integrations
